court: Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit

issues.label: Subject-matter jurisdiction
issues.why: The court must confirm federal-question jurisdiction over RLUIPA and constitutional claims.

issues.label: Proper defendants identified
issues.why: The court must determine which officials are proper parties given roles, substitutions, and capacities.

issues.label: Service and personal jurisdiction
issues.why: The court must ensure each defendant was properly served and is subject to the court’s jurisdiction.

issues.label: Venue propriety
issues.why: The court must confirm the chosen federal district is the correct venue for the events and parties.

issues.label: PLRA exhaustion
issues.why: The court must decide whether Roberts exhausted available administrative remedies as required by the PLRA.

issues.label: PLRA availability exceptions
issues.why: If Roberts did not exhaust, the court must assess whether remedies were effectively unavailable.

issues.label: PLRA physical injury bar
issues.why: For compensatory damages for mental/emotional injury, the court must apply 42 U.S.C. § 1997e(e) and consider claimed food poisoning injuries.

issues.label: Statute of limitations
issues.why: The court must determine whether any claims are time-barred based on accrual and applicable limitations periods.

issues.label: Continuing violation doctrine
issues.why: The court must decide whether repeated Ramadan denials constitute a continuing violation affecting timeliness.

issues.label: Proper pleading verification
issues.why: The court must determine the legal effect of the later-verified amended complaint on summary-judgment evidence.

issues.label: Summary-judgment standard
issues.why: The court must view evidence in Roberts’s favor and identify genuine disputes of material fact.

issues.label: Evidentiary admissibility
issues.why: The court must consider whether pro se submissions are admissible or can be reduced to admissible form.

issues.label: Magistrate discovery ruling review
issues.why: The court must address any preserved objections/appeal of the motion-to-compel denial affecting the record.

issues.label: Discovery sufficiency under Rule 56(d)
issues.why: The court must consider whether Roberts needed additional discovery to oppose summary judgment.

issues.label: RLUIPA applicability to VDOC
issues.why: The court must confirm that VDOC receives federal financial assistance triggering RLUIPA coverage.

issues.label: RLUIPA protected exercise
issues.why: The court must decide whether Roberts’s Kashrut-supervision and Ramadan-fasting practices are religious exercise under RLUIPA.

issues.label: Sincerity of belief
issues.why: Although not disputed, the court must recognize sincerity as the threshold for Free Exercise/RLUIPA protection.

issues.label: RLUIPA substantial burden
issues.why: The court must decide whether forcing a choice between OJKD and fasting substantially burdened Roberts’s religious exercise.

issues.label: RLUIPA compelling interest
issues.why: If burden shown, the court must evaluate VDOC’s asserted interests (food safety, logistics, procurement timing) as compelling.

issues.label: RLUIPA least restrictive means
issues.why: The court must decide whether denying Ramadan-compliant OJKD in 2020 was the least restrictive means versus alternatives.

issues.label: RLUIPA individualized assessment
issues.why: The court must consider whether the denial rested on generalized assertions or an individualized evaluation of Roberts’s request.

issues.label: RLUIPA causation and liability
issues.why: The court must determine which defendants personally caused or were responsible for the burden imposed.

issues.label: RLUIPA remedies scope
issues.why: The court must determine what remedies RLUIPA allows against officials/agency (injunctive/declaratory vs damages).

issues.label: RLUIPA individual-capacity damages
issues.why: The court must apply controlling precedent on whether RLUIPA permits damages against officials in their individual capacities.

issues.label: Eleventh Amendment immunity
issues.why: The court must bar damages claims against state officials in official capacities absent waiver or abrogation.

issues.label: Ex parte Young exception
issues.why: The court must decide whether prospective injunctive relief against current officials is permissible notwithstanding immunity.

issues.label: Mootness of injunctive relief
issues.why: The court must decide whether VDOC’s 2021 Ramadan-compliant OJKD moots prospective relief requests.

issues.label: Voluntary cessation exception
issues.why: Even with policy change, the court must assess whether VDOC could revert, keeping injunctive claims live.

issues.label: Capable-of-repetition exception
issues.why: The court must consider whether Ramadan’s recurring nature makes the dispute likely to recur yet evade review.

issues.label: Mootness of declaratory relief
issues.why: The court must decide whether a declaration about past conduct remains a live controversy after policy change.

issues.label: Standing for each remedy
issues.why: The court must ensure Roberts has injury-in-fact, traceability, and redressability for damages and equitable relief.

issues.label: Free Exercise threshold burden
issues.why: The court must determine whether the 2020 accommodation denial imposed a constitutionally cognizable burden on religious practice.

issues.label: Turner reasonableness test
issues.why: For prison restrictions, the court must apply Turner/O’Lone factors to assess reasonableness of the policy/decision.

issues.label: Alternative means factor
issues.why: Under Turner, the court must evaluate whether Roberts retained alternative means to practice his religion.

issues.label: Impact on prison resources
issues.why: Turner requires assessing the effect of accommodation on staff, budgets, ordering, and food-safety operations.

issues.label: Ready alternatives factor
issues.why: The court must consider whether obvious, easy alternatives (e.g., safe bagging protocols) existed at de minimis cost.

issues.label: Food-safety justification scrutiny
issues.why: The court must assess whether the Four-Hour Rule and safety concerns rationally support denying OJKD Ramadan meals in 2020.

issues.label: Six-month switchback policy
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether delaying return to OJKD burdens religion and whether it is reasonably related to penological interests.

issues.label: Causation of illness harms
issues.why: The court must decide whether defendants’ actions foreseeably caused Roberts to store food and become ill, affecting damages.

issues.label: Qualified immunity framework
issues.why: The court must decide (1) constitutional violation and (2) clearly established law for each individual-capacity claim.

issues.label: Clearly established Free Exercise right
issues.why: The court must determine whether precedent clearly required accommodating a Muslim inmate’s sincerely held kosher-supervision beliefs during Ramadan.

issues.label: Level of generality in QI
issues.why: The court must frame the right with appropriate specificity, not too broadly or too narrowly, when applying qualified immunity.

issues.label: Personal involvement for §1983
issues.why: The court must determine each defendant’s personal participation or supervisory liability for constitutional violations.

issues.label: Supervisory liability limits
issues.why: The court must apply standards for supervisory liability (knowledge, deliberate indifference, causation) rather than respondeat superior.

issues.label: Official policy or custom
issues.why: The court must identify whether the challenged conduct was policy-driven (menus, Four-Hour Rule, switchback rule) versus ad hoc decisions.

issues.label: Establishment Clause theory
issues.why: The court must clarify whether Roberts alleges preferential treatment of Judaism or excessive entanglement via rabbinical supervision requirements.

issues.label: Establishment Clause prison standard
issues.why: The court must apply the appropriate Establishment Clause test in prisons (e.g., neutrality/endorsement/entanglement considerations).

issues.label: No-aid/neutrality concerns
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether providing OJKD or denying it to a Muslim constitutes impermissible religious favoritism or neutrality failure.

issues.label: Equal Protection classification
issues.why: The court must determine the relevant comparator groups (Jewish OJKD inmates vs Muslim inmates) and the classification at issue.

issues.label: Similarly situated comparators
issues.why: Equal protection requires deciding whether Roberts was similarly situated to Jewish inmates receiving OJKD accommodations.

issues.label: Discriminatory intent requirement
issues.why: The court must decide whether any differential treatment was motivated by intentional discrimination rather than neutral policy constraints.

issues.label: Equal Protection level of scrutiny
issues.why: The court must determine whether strict scrutiny or rational-basis applies given religion-related discrimination allegations in prison context.

issues.label: Rational basis for disparity
issues.why: If no intent/strict scrutiny, the court must assess whether operational/logistical reasons rationally explain different treatment.

issues.label: Availability of nominal damages
issues.why: The court must determine whether Roberts can recover nominal damages for past constitutional violations despite moot injunctive claims.

issues.label: Punitive damages standard
issues.why: The court must decide whether defendants acted with evil motive or reckless indifference to support punitive damages under §1983.

issues.label: Compensatory damages proof
issues.why: The court must determine whether Roberts has evidence of actual injury (medical harm, costs) attributable to constitutional violations.

issues.label: Declaratory judgment discretion
issues.why: Even if jurisdiction exists, the court must decide whether declaratory relief is appropriate and not merely advisory.

issues.label: Prospective relief scope
issues.why: If not moot, the court must tailor any injunction narrowly under the PLRA need-narrowness-intrusiveness requirements.

issues.label: PLRA injunction findings
issues.why: The court must make specific findings under 18 U.S.C. § 3626 for any prospective relief affecting prison operations.

issues.label: Proper defendant for injunction
issues.why: The court must ensure any Ex parte Young injunction runs against the official with authority to implement diet policies.

issues.label: Policy-change evidence weight
issues.why: The court must consider whether post-2020 accommodations show feasibility, undercutting least-restrictive-means/Turner defenses.

issues.label: State-law deference limits
issues.why: The court must balance deference to prison administrators with the heightened scrutiny RLUIPA imposes.

issues.label: Relief against former director
issues.why: The court must determine how substitution affects official-capacity claims and prospective relief against current VDOC leadership.

issues.label: Attorney’s fees availability
issues.why: The court must consider whether fees could be awarded under §1988 or RLUIPA if Roberts later obtains relief.

issues.label: Appellate standard of review
issues.why: The court must apply de novo review for summary judgment and legal immunity determinations, and abuse-of-discretion for discovery rulings.
